Southpark is poking fun at a few ideas here. They're making fun of people pretending to be part of an ethnicity and a culture they're not. They're doing this through shock value - the guy saying nigga, annoying stereotypes - the voices of the people in the ad, and through exaggeration. Separately, they're also mocking the aesthetic and branding of companies like 23 and me. The clean white background and logo are supposed to show us that gene sequencing companies, while attempting to distinguish themselves as pioneers or creators through branding, are completely formulaic too. However, they don't go much beyond any of this. Southpark never bothers to, for example, explain why people want to be part of an ethnicity or culture they're not. The answer to this might be the homogenization and even destruction of these white people's culture, as well as the romanticism of foreign ethnicities. In a deeper sense, people associating themselves with other cultures is a symptom of the nihilism increasingly pervasive in our society. But Southpark doesn't talk about any of this. All these Southpark skits are are conversation starters; not necessarily containing much content themselves.
